ticket.title: userRepo.ts: ILIKE search on encrypted PII columns can never match — :1017 and :1061 compare ciphertext to a pattern

repo.test_runner: vitest (run one file with `npx vitest run <file>` from Blockchain/Dev/services/auth; setupFiles ./vitest.setup.ts)
repo.typescript: strict, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, esModuleInterop, module commonjs, target ES2022; the product file's imports at the tip are: import { User, UserRole, VerificationLevel, DB_STATUS_TO_DOMAIN } from '../types'; | import { query } from '../db'; | import { logger } from '../utils/logger'; | import { | import { subjectDeks } from '../services/subjectDeks'; | import { isInfrastructureDbError } from './dbErrors'; | import { ServiceUnavailableError } from '../middleware/errorHandler';

defect_line.text: conditions.push(`(email ILIKE $${idx} OR first_name ILIKE $${idx} OR last_name ILIKE $${idx} OR display_name ILIKE $${idx})`);
expected_plus: // KS-1168 (Kam 2026-09-16, `secuura-ks1168-ilike-search-on-encrypted-pii`,
// option a): EXACT-only search. `email`, `first_name`, `last_name` and
// `display_name` are all written through `encryptPiiCol` (see createUser at
// :671 and :703-705), so the old `ILIKE '%term%'` compared a pattern against
// per-row ciphertext: it never errored and never matched, and an admin
// searching for a real user was told there was no such user.
// `email_lookup_hash` is the deterministic HMAC column getUserByEmail
// already uses, so the listing now searches by EXACT email. The three name
// columns leave the predicate: a substring search over a keyed hash is not
// possible, and giving them lookup columns of their own is a migration.
// countUsersInner below carries the same block, and must - the page and the
// total that labels it have to ask one question.
conditions.push(`email_lookup_hash = $${idx}`);
values.push(lookupHash(search.toLowerCase().trim()));
// KS-1168 (Kam 2026-09-16, option a, "EXACT-only search"): the same change
// as listUsersInner above, and it has to be the same change - a total
// computed from a different predicate disagrees with the page it labels.
// The fuller note on why an ILIKE over these columns can never match is
// there; this is its twin.
conditions.push(`email_lookup_hash = $${idx}`);
values.push(lookupHash(search.toLowerCase().trim()));
* KS-1168 (Kam 2026-09-16, option a, "EXACT-only search"): the SAME rule now
* governs the user LISTING. `listUsersInner` and `countUsersInner` resolve
* their `search` term through `lookupHash` against `email_lookup_hash` too,
* instead of an `ILIKE` over the encrypted `email` / `first_name` /
* `last_name` / `display_name` columns, which could never match.
defect_line.sites_rule: every site with must_change=true MUST be changed by the product hunk (its text appears as a '-' line); the checker refuses a diff that leaves one untouched (A3b) before any test runs
red_cells: RED 1: listUsers builds no ILIKE predicate
RED 2: countUsers builds no ILIKE predicate
RED 3: listUsers matches email_lookup_hash with the exact lookup hash
RED 4: countUsers matches email_lookup_hash with the exact lookup hash
